metadata.title: Fill The Template. Don't Write It.
metadata.subtitle: The Notify-Templates Skill
metadata.purpose: Take apart the notify-templates skill: explain why Claude fills three fixed message formats from data at hand instead of drafting each alert, evaluate the choice to route by written threshold rather than judgment, and name what a batch-then-append design leaves uncovered. Land the carry-out that Claude fills templates from data it already has, and a sweep becomes one summary and one append, never one call per SKU.

beats.narration_text: Here's the assumption: Claude writes each alert from scratch, choosing words case by case. It doesn't. It fills a fixed template. Identical output — not authorship. Does Claude fill the low-stock alert template?

beats.narration_text: A Claude skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one — notify-templates — carries three fixed formats: a low-stock Slack alert, a supplier email, an escalation for human review. Fill the slots from data at hand, append the result, stop. The file rules out a subagent explicitly. They optimized for a reproducible append over adaptive judgment.

production_viz.label: THREE TEMPLATES, NO SUBAGENT
production_viz.caption: fill the slots, then append — never a subagent

beats.narration_text: Routing is written down too — no interpretation. Default lands in ops. An active stockout on a top SKU adds an at-here. Over twenty-five thousand dollars skips the channel — straight to a purchasing lead. Past one hundred thousand outstanding, or a suspected duplicate order, finance is pinged. Cross a threshold; the message names which. Routed by rule, not taste — auditable, at the cost of adaptability.

production_viz.label: WHERE IT'S ROUTED
production_viz.caption: over $25k goes to a lead, not the channel

beats.narration_text: A daily sweep works the same way — batched. One summary message, not one per SKU — even when the task says notify each, every line lands in a single batch append. Sending is one write to an outbox file: JSON, one line per notification. Past two tool calls to send an alert and something has already gone wrong. Same data, same template, same append — every time. Legible bill, legible paper trail — over per-SKU immediacy.

production_viz.label: BATCH, DON'T SPAM
production_viz.caption: same data, same template, same append — every time

beats.narration_text: Claude doesn't write these alerts — it fills three fixed templates from data it already has. A sweep becomes one summary and one append, never one call per SKU.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: I'm designing a notify-templates skill for an inventory ops workflow — three fixed message formats (low-stock Slack alert, supplier email, escalation for human review) that Claude fills from inventory data instead of drafting from scratch. (1) Draft the three SKILL.md templates as fillable slots — name each slot, describe the data feeding it, and explain why fixing the format matters more than clever wording. (2) Write a routing table: default to an ops channel; add an at-here for an active stockout on a top SKU; jump straight to a purchasing lead over twenty-five thousand dollars; escalate to finance past one hundred thousand outstanding or on a suspected duplicate order. Name every threshold. (3) Show the batch rule: for a daily sweep across many SKUs, one summary message and one append to a JSON outbox — never one call per SKU — with a two-tool-call ceiling per alert. Go deeper: ask the same model where a fixed template forces the wrong message — a partial shipment that's only half a stockout, a supplier who bounces the email, a threshold-crossing SKU that also has a returns issue — and show which of those the notify-templates design would silently mishandle.
